name: Flexential Salt Lake City - Fair Park

source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

profile.reading: This Flexential cluster spans Colorado (Aurora, Centennial, Denver, Englewood), Utah (Lindon, Salt Lake City, West Jordan), and Nevada (Las Vegas, North Las Vegas), the historic Western United States footprint of ViaWest. According to Flexential own company history page, ViaWest was founded in 1999 and built a strong regional presence across the Western US. In 2017 Peak 10 purchased ViaWest, merging the two regionally dominant data center providers, and the combined company rebranded as Flexential in 2018. Flexential operates 40 plus data centers across 18 national markets as of its current company page, backed by a 2.1 billion dollar inaugural securitization completed in 2021, one of the largest data center green bond asset backed security issuances at the time. No building specific address or individual MW figures for these particular registry rows were located in available sourcing this session.

reading.body:
Flexential Salt Lake City - Fair Park in Salt Lake City, Utah, is operated by Flexential, but no IT capacity in megawatts has been published for this facility.

Without a published capacity figure, the facility cannot be sized against other data centers in this collection, or judged for whether it could plausibly host AI training infrastructure, which typically requires tens of megawatts and up. What is on record is the facility's location and operator, not its scale.

Flexential Salt Lake City - Fair Park holds 4 published certifications: SOC 1 Type 2 (audited controls over financial reporting processes), SOC 2 Type 2 (audited controls over security, availability, and confidentiality, tested over time rather than at a point), HITRUST (a healthcare-focused security framework built on top of HIPAA), SSAE 18 (the attestation standard underlying SOC reports). Together these qualify the facility for regulated workloads spanning security auditing, payments, and healthcare data, though which specific tenants rely on which certification is not disclosed.

Utah has 9 facilities mapped in this site's dataset, of which 8 publish a megawatt figure, totaling 51.69 MW.
